explanation: Price above MC leaves allocative inefficiency. Output below minimum-ATC quantity leaves excess capacity and productive inefficiency.

prompt: A monopolistically competitive firm's demand becomes more elastic after entry of close substitutes. Which broad long-run process is this part of?

options.label: E
options.text: Entry eroding short-run economic profit toward zero

explanation: Entry gives buyers more substitutes and reduces incumbent demand. Economic profits are competed away.

prompt: Advertising successfully differentiates a firm's product and raises its demand in the short run. Which conclusion is safest under the CED?

options.label: C
options.text: Advertising converts the market to monopoly

options.label: D
options.text: Temporary profit; entry restores zero long-run profit

explanation: Advertising can differentiate products while firms earn a normal return. Free entry and exit still drive economic profit to zero.

prompt: A market contains many differentiated brands. Some firms currently earn profit and others losses. Which statement is most consistent with Topic 4.4?

options.label: A
options.text: All firms must already earn zero profit

options.label: D
options.text: The market must be an oligopoly

options.label: E
options.text: Entry and exit restore zero long-run profit

explanation: Different short-run demand and cost conditions permit positive profit, a loss, or zero profit.

prompt: Which graph feature would distinguish long-run monopolistic competition from a long-run competitive firm?

options.label: A
options.text: P above ATC with positive profit

options.label: C
options.text: D–ATC tangency left of minimum ATC, with P > MC

explanation: The long-run graph has demand tangent to ATC before its minimum and price above MC. It shows zero profit, excess capacity, and allocative inefficiency together.

options.label: B

reference: PRD-3.B | PRD-3.B.10 Quality-Control Audits Audit 1 — CED Alignment and Scope All 100 questions are confined to Topic 4.4 Monopolistic Competition and Essential Knowledge PRD-3.B.10. Coverage is limited to differentiated products, advertising as a means of differentiation, positive/negative/zero economic profit in the short run, free entry and exit driving profit to zero in the long run, excess capacity because output is below the ATC-minimizing quantity, and allocative inefficiency because P > MC. Graphs are embedded throughout: short-run profit, short-run loss, long-run zero-profit tangency, excess capacity, P > MC allocative inefficiency, entry reducing an incumbent's demand, exit increasing a remaining firm's demand, and advertising/product differentiation. Topic 4.5 oligopoly and game theory is intentionally excluded. No concentration-ratio, strategic interaction, dominant-strategy, Nash-equilibrium, or payoff-matrix content is used. Audit 2 — Construction, Difficulty, and Answer Integrity Question count: 100. Difficulty distribution: 33 Easy, 40 Medium, 27 Hard. Each item has five answer choices and one keyed answer. Correct-answer positions are balanced exactly: A=20, B=20, C=20, D=20, E=20. Numerical items were recomputed using profit=(P-ATC)×Q, loss=(ATC-P)×Q, excess capacity=Q at minimum ATC minus actual long-run Q, and allocative wedge=P-MC. Hard questions integrate short-run profit/loss with long-run entry/exit, and distinguish zero economic profit from allocative and productive efficiency without importing Topic 4.5.
